processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Binary Fe-Al alloys were prepared by vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles using Fe of 99.99% purity (purified by zone melting to minimise impurity content) and Al of 99.999% purity. Levitation melting was used only for selected alloys.
The melt was solidified in Cu moulds to obtain rods usually with 18 mm diameter. The sample is used in the as-cast state, i.e. without any subsequent heat treatment.

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline, coarse-grained as-cast Fe-6 at.% Al alloy; the as-cast condition contains no second phases.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression specimens 5×5×10 mm3; cylindrical tensile specimens turned according to DIN 50125
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Polycrystalline as-cast alloys tested in compression (0.2% proof stress, total straining of at least 5%) and in tension at room temperature and -100 °C.

characterization_methods.purpose: Determination of the alloy compositions (real Al content and impurity contents) listed in Table 1.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The nominal 6 at.% Al alloy has a real Al content of 6.0 at.% (3.0 wt.-%), with C 50 wt.ppm and Si 70 wt.ppm as impurities.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: specimens etched by an alcoholic 10% nitric acid solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal grain boundaries, precipitates and the grain structure of the polycrystalline alloys.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Polycrystalline as-cast alloys show a coarse grain structure of the order of 1 mm; the as-cast alloy contained no second phases.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature and -100 °C; strain rates 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^-2 s^-1; specimens 5×5×10 mm3
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the yield stress as a function of Al content for the polycrystalline alloys.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The yield stress increases linearly with increasing Al content for as-cast polycrystalline alloys up to 18 at.% Al; usually two specimens of each alloy were tested, differing by 3% at most.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: cylindrical specimens turned according to German standard DIN 50125
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature and -100 °C; strain rates between 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^-2 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Study the ductility and fracture behaviour of the polycrystalline alloys as a function of Al content.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The most ductile Fe-4%Al shows a yield stress drop at -100 °C, which was also observed for Fe-6%Al.

unmapped_findings: Fe-6%Al as-cast composition (Table 1): nominal 6 at.% Al; real Al content 6.0 at.% (3.0 wt.-%); impurities C 50 wt.ppm and Si 70 wt.ppm.
The polycrystalline as-cast Fe-6%Al alloy showed a yield stress drop at -100 °C; only Fe-4%Al (the most ductile alloy) and Fe-6%Al produced such low-temperature yield stress drops.

For the as-cast polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys (0-18 at.% Al, which include Fe-6%Al) the room-temperature yield stress increases linearly with Al content; the solid-solution hardening coefficient is about 2.2 GPa, consistent with Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys.
The tensile yield stress equals the compressive yield stress for the studied polycrystalline as-cast alloys at the same rate and temperature.
At -100 °C the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength of the polycrystalline as-cast alloys are higher than those at room temperature by about 80 MPa.
